lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Four days after another narrow collapse, the Leafs are skating into Saturday with a season that refuses to settle. The 3-2 loss to the Mammoth left Toronto at 8-7, 10th in the Eastern Conference and seven points out of the pace - a 1- game losing streak, but a larger warning about a club surrendering ground in the middle of the pack. The most encouraging development is John Tavares' likely return against Montreal after practicing in a regular sweater. He brings two goals and five assists in seven games before his lower-body injury, plus the kind of net-front presence Toronto has missed. The wrinkle is significant: Tavares will return as a left winger beside Nick Paul and William Nylander, while rookie Gavin McKenna moves down the top power play. Saturday's 7 p.m. meeting with the Canadiens is the test: can Tavares' return turn possession into pressure?

the_latest.headline: Leafs fell to Mammoth 3-2
the_latest.dek: Toronto dropped to 8-7, extending an inconsistent stretch since returning from its Western road trip. The 3-2 loss also left the Leafs sitting 10th in the Eastern Conference, increasing the pressure to turn narrow defeats into points.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's offseason has already supplied the first hard truth: good gloves cannot hide a roster that finished 79-83, even if that record placed the Blue Jays second in the AL East. The club's American League Team Gold Glove, announced Friday, is an honor - and an indictment: Toronto led the league in errors while receiving no individual Gold Glove winner. That is not a foundation to discard, but it is hardly a finished product. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. remains the central figure, now back home in the Dominican Republic after gifting his mother a Lexus and reminding everyone that the franchise's biggest star still carries its emotional weight. The serious work is on the mound. Toronto must decide whether to spend boldly on rotation help or gamble on internal answers. Watch for reunions in free agency and a decisive push to fortify the 2027 rotation before camp opens.

the_latest.headline: Which familiar faces could Blue Jays reunite with in free agency?
the_latest.dek: After a 79-83 finish and a last-place offensive showing in home runs, Toronto has clear work to do before 2027. Familiar free agents could offer needed stability in the rotation and lineup, but each reunion must fit a roster reshaped by recent trades.

the_latest.dek: With Toronto's season over at 79-83, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is turning to family as the offseason begins. He surprised his mother, Riquelma Ramos, with a luxury Lexus in the Dominican Republic, sharing an emotional message alongside the gift.

the_latest.headline: Louis Varland, Andy Pages among Super 2 arbitration eligibles
the_latest.dek: Varland's Super 2 status could give Toronto an added salary decision during an offseason focused on reshaping a 79-83 club. With arbitration costs rising for players who narrowly qualify, the Blue Jays must weigh his value as a closer against flexibility elsewhere on the roster.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A team missing Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley walked into Milwaukee, absorbed a 15-point punch, then answered with the sort of second-half ferocity that travels. Alijah Martin's career-high 27 points powered Toronto past the Bucks 121-107, with the second-year guard drilling 6 of 7 from three after entering the night 6-for-27 from deep in his NBA career. RJ Barrett supplied 27 as well, while Toronto's growing appetite for disruption - the "cobra, shark, eagle" defense - turned pressure into momentum. The Raptors are 5-4, third in the Atlantic Division, and riding a one-game winning streak after alternating wins and losses across their last four. That is progress, not proof. The injury list remains the hinge. Monday's 7:30 p.m. ET meeting with Memphis will show whether Milwaukee was a breakthrough or merely a marvelous night of emergency arithmetic.

the_latest.headline: Raptors beat Bucks 121-107
the_latest.dek: Toronto rallied from a 15-point deficit to outscore Milwaukee 70-47 after halftime, improving to 5-4 and strengthening its hold on third in the Atlantic. Alijah Martin and RJ Barrett each scored 27 points, while Jamal Shead added a career-high 16 assists in a short-handed win.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders finally look like a team with a pulse - but the margin for error is shrinking. Washington's 27-10 demolition of Philadelphia on Nov. 1 lifted it to 2-4-1, kept it second in the NFC East, and snapped a four-game stretch without a win. Now comes the less forgiving part: the receiving room is being stripped bare. Dyami Brown is out with a calf injury, Treylon Burks is sidelined by a foot injury, and Washington may have only four active receivers against Los Angeles, leaving Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams to carry the passing load. The reward for that shortage is a Rams defense expected to welcome back Myles Garrett - a nasty test for an offense trying to build momentum. Sunday at 1 p.m. against Los Angeles is the measuring stick: protect the quarterback, replace the missing targets, and prove that Philadelphia was a beginning, not a detour.

the_latest.headline: Commanders beat Eagles 27-10
the_latest.dek: The victory moved Washington to 2-4-1 and kept the Commanders within two games of first place in a crowded NFC East. A defense that pressured Philadelphia on 46.5% of dropbacks now has a chance to build its first winning streak of the season against the Rams.

article.title: Tavares Returns as Leafs Face Canadiens
paragraphs: John Tavares is back in the Maple Leafs lineup tonight, moving to left wing as Toronto hosts Montreal at 7:00 p.m. ET on Sportsnet. The Leafs enter at 8-7, 10th in the Eastern Conference, with Sergei Bobrovsky projected against Cam Fowler. Toronto's netminder is 3-6-2 with a 3.26 goals-against average, while Fowler is 6-0-1 at 2.38.

The Raptors are 5-4 after beating the Bucks 121-107, led by Alijah Martin and RJ Barrett with 27 points each. Jakob Poeltl had 11 rebounds and Jamal Shead 16 assists; Memphis visits Monday at 7:30 p.m. ET. The Blue Jays are looking toward free agency, with familiar reunions under discussion. The Commanders, 2-4-1 and second in the NFC East, face the Rams Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox without receivers Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks, both ruled out.
